## Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Evidence reviewed
Only one file was present in the evidence directory: `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames). No IDS/Suricata alert exports or other artifacts were supplied, so all attribution below is derived from packet behavior, not a signature match.

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** | Dominant local talker in all conversations |
| MAC | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.1.21.58` ↔ `arp.src.hw_mac`), confirmed same MAC on DHCP request and on the host's link-local fallback address 169.254.227.202 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (also broadcasts NetBIOS name **WIN11OFFICE**) | NBNS name registrations from 10.1.21.58; DHCP option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-ES9F3ML` tied to MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2 |

LAN scope: 10.1.21.0/24, gateway 10.1.21.1 (MAC 00:04:c1:be:8c:d4), domain controller 10.1.21.2 (MAC 14:b3:1f:2d:ce:69), AD domain **win11office.com** (DC `WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com`).

### Malware family
**Attribution confidence: behavioral (not signature-confirmed)** — no IDS/Suricata alerts were provided with this evidence set.

The victim's traffic shows a classic **fake-verification / TDS (traffic-distribution-system) fingerprinting gate**, consistent with the delivery pattern used by ClickFix-style stealer/loader campaigns (e.g., families such as Lumma Stealer, Vidar, or similar commodity infostealers that use this exact "browser-fingerprint-then-serve-payload" gate). The strongest evidence is a plaintext HTTP check-in to `whitepepper.su`:

- `GET /api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&agent=Chrome`
- `POST /api/set_agent?...&agent=Chrome&act=log` — POST body is a full browser fingerprint (platform, userAgent, WebGL vendor/renderer "AMD Radeon R9 200 Series", canvas fingerprint hash) sent as urlencoded form data.
- The same sequence repeats seconds later tagged `agent=Edge`, i.e., the malicious page/script re-checked-in under a second spoofed browser identity.

This fingerprint-harvest-then-log pattern is the signature behavior of an anti-bot/anti-sandbox gate that decides whether to serve the real payload to a given visitor — it is not itself a RAT C2 protocol, but it sits directly in the infection chain immediately before/alongside contact with several other freshly-registered lookalike domains, which is why the host is assessed as compromised rather than merely having visited a scam page. Because the remaining suspicious hosts communicate over TLS 1.3, the payload contents (installer/loader binary) could not be recovered from the capture — no plaintext executable was observed, so no file name or SHA256 could be grounded in evidence for the payload itself.

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / gate endpoints (IP:port)**
| Indicator | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `153.92.1.49:80` (whitepepper.su) | Cleartext HTTP `set_agent` fingerprint check-in/log sequence described above, two full check-in cycles ~7s apart |
| `153.92.1.49:443` | Same host also contacted over TLS (SNI `whitepepper.su`) |

**Suspicious/malicious domains** (all newly-observed, non-Microsoft/Google infrastructure, resolved and contacted by the victim only)
| Domain | Resolved IP(s) | First seen (t+sec) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| whitepepper.su | 153.92.1.49 | 92.3 | DNS A record + HTTP requests above |
| hiyter.com | 104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145 | 45.3 | DNS query/response; TLS SNI `cloudflare-ech.com`-fronted contact to 104.21.22.231 |
| media.megafilehub4.lat | 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 | 45.8 | DNS query/response; TLS SNI `media.megafilehub4.lat` in ClientHello |
| arch.filemegahab4.sbs | 104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13 | 48.3 | DNS query/response; TLS to 104.21.46.67 (16 MB transferred, the single largest conversation in the capture — consistent with a payload/archive download) |
| whooptm.cyou | 62.72.32.156 | 90.3 | DNS query/response; TLS session to 62.72.32.156 |
| holiday-forever.cc | 80.97.160.24 | 122.8 | DNS query/response; TLS session to 80.97.160.24 |
| communicationfirewall-security.cc | 104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109 | 126.5 | DNS query/response; TLS session to 104.21.9.36 |

**Malicious URLs (cleartext, fully observed)**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (POST, fingerprint exfil)

**Transferred file / SHA256:** None could be grounded. All traffic to the other suspicious IPs (megafilehub4.lat, filemegahab4.sbs, holiday-forever.cc, whooptm.cyou, communicationfirewall-security.cc) is TLS-encrypted; no decryption keys were available, and no plaintext file transfer or hash-recoverable object was present in the capture.

**Benign context (not indicators)**
- Microsoft/Windows telemetry and services: `login.microsoftonline.com`, `login.live.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `v10/v20.events.data.microsoft.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `officeapps.live.com`, `ecs.office.com`, `edge.microsoft.com`, MSN/Bing content domains.
- Google services: `clients2/4/6.google.com`, `accounts.google.com`, `gstatic.com`, `googleapis.com` family, YouTube/Drive/Play.
- CDN/analytics: `cloudflareinsights.com`, `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `assets.adobedtm.com`.
- AD/domain traffic: LDAP, Kerberos, DCE/RPC (samr, lsarpc, drsuapi) between 10.1.21.58 and 10.1.21.2 — normal domain-joined workstation activity.
- NBNS/mDNS/SSDP/LLMNR local discovery broadcasts.

### Summary
The Windows 11 workstation **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (10.1.21.58, MAC 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2), logged in as domain user **gwyatt**, contacted a cluster of newly-registered lookalike domains (`hiyter.com`, `media.megafilehub4.lat`, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, `whooptm.cyou`, `holiday-forever.cc`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`) and a browser-fingerprinting gate at `whitepepper.su`, which logged full WebGL/canvas/device fingerprints under spoofed "Chrome" and "Edge" agent identities before further contact continued to the other domains. This is consistent behaviorally with a fake-verification/TDS gate used to gate delivery of a commodity infostealer or loader; the actual payload transfer (16 MB to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` via Cloudflare) is TLS-encrypted and its file name/hash could not be recovered from this capture alone. Attribution to a specific named malware family is behavioral, not signature-confirmed — no IDS/Suricata alerts accompanied this evidence set.
